Laptop Log Collector  v1.8
======================================================================

1. What this is
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A one-click log collection tool for laptop testers. Tick the items you need;
the tool copies the logs, system information, crash dumps, power and
performance data into one folder and generates an HTML report that can be
handed straight to engineering.

No installation, no network access, no changes to system settings.
The interface and all generated reports are in English.

2. Requirements
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit), any display language
- Portable: a single exe, no .NET / Python / runtime required
- Run as administrator recommended (otherwise dumps, WER, energy report,
  sleep study and Wi-Fi history are skipped)

3. Three steps
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Double-click LogCollector.exe
2) Tick what to collect (the common set is already ticked)
3) Optionally change the output folder: type a path, or press "Browse..."
   to pick one (the default is Desktop\LogCollection)
4) Click "Start collection" and wait for the progress bar

An "Open the HTML report now?" prompt appears when done.

Avoid using the machine while collecting, especially for the performance
and energy items.

4. What each item collects
----------------------------------------------------------------------
[Basics]
  System event log + key event analysis  BSOD, unexpected shutdown, driver
                                         and hardware errors
  Application event log                  app crashes and hangs
  All event log files (.evtx)            every .evtx under winevt\Logs, folder
                                         structure mirrored incl. empty folders
  System info and hardware details       model, serial, BIOS, CPU, memory,
                                         graphics, battery, problem devices
  Drivers and devices                    driver versions, signing, driver
                                         store, devices with error codes
  Processes, services and startup        current runtime state
  Patches and installed software         environment change history
  msinfo32 full report (slow)            more detail, may hang (off by default)

[Crashes and dumps]
  Blue screen dumps (Minidump)           copies every .dmp in the Minidump folder
  WER crash reports (full folder)        mirrors C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER
                                         with its structure; needs admin
  Live kernel reports                    mirrors C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports
                                         (GPU hangs/timeouts without a BSOD); needs admin
  Full memory dump (MEMORY.DMP)          only if the system already created it
  Process memory dump (GB)               full dump of a running process

[Power and battery]
  Battery health report                  design/full capacity, cycles, drain curve
  Power settings and wake sources        sleep/hibernate/display/disk timeouts,
                                         lid and power button action, hybrid sleep
  Energy report (60 s audit)             needs admin
  Sleep study + system power report      powercfg /sleepstudy and powercfg /spr
                                         (sleepstudy-report.html); needs admin

[Performance]
  Performance sampling (30 s)            CPU, free memory, disk busy, MHz, battery
  Graphics and display (dxdiag)          GPU driver, display modes, TDR records

[Network]
  Network configuration snapshot         IP, routes, DNS, Wi-Fi, proxy, TCP
  Wi-Fi connection history               connect/disconnect timeline, needs admin

[Storage]
  Disk and SMART health                  health, temperature, power-on hours, wear

[Setup and component logs]
  Windows setup logs (Panther)           mirrors C:\Windows\Panther: setupact.log,
                                         setupapi, migration and rollback data
                                         (can be ~2 GB; needs admin)
  Windows component logs                 mirrors C:\Windows\Logs: CBS, DISM,
                                         WindowsUpdate, WinRE, MoSetup
  Driver INF and setup logs              mirrors C:\Windows\INF incl. setupapi.dev.log
                                         and every installed driver INF

[Other]
  Extra log folder                       logs of the application under test

5. Output
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Default output folder: Desktop\LogCollection\
Each run creates a folder named <BIOS serial>_<timestamp>, for example
N4N0CV01760013H_20261107-162543. The serial number is read from the BIOS
(Win32_BIOS.SerialNumber). If the BIOS returns a placeholder such as
"Default string", the model name is used instead and the log says so.
The timestamp keeps several runs on the same machine apart.

The folder contains:

  report.html            start here: key findings, event timeline,
                         hardware, battery and power settings
  All_Content.html       every text file in one browsable page
  Collection_Info.txt    what was collected, status and how to read it
  10_System_Logs\        System.evtx + key_events.csv
  11_Application_Logs\   Application.evtx + app_crash_events.csv
  12_All_Event_Logs\     all .evtx files: Logs\ is an exact mirror of winevt\Logs
                         (empty folders included) when run as administrator;
                         otherwise Channels\ holds one .evtx per exported channel
  20_System_Info\        systeminfo.txt / hardware_info.csv / system_summary.txt
  21_Drivers_Devices\    drivers.csv / driver_store.txt / problem_devices.txt
  22_Runtime_Snapshot\   processes, services, startup items
  23_Patches_Software\
  30_Crash_Dumps\        blue screen dmp files
  31_WER_Reports\        WER\ is a mirror of C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER
  32_Memory_Dump\        MEMORY.DMP
  33_Process_Dump\       process memory dump
  34_LiveKernel_Reports\ LiveKernelReports\ mirrors C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports
  35_Setup_Panther\      Panther\ mirrors C:\Windows\Panther
  36_Windows_Logs\       Logs\ mirrors C:\Windows\Logs
  37_Inf_Drivers\        INF\ mirrors C:\Windows\INF
  40_Battery\ 41_Power_Settings\ 42_Energy_Report\ 43_Sleep_Study\
  50_Performance\ 60_Display_GPU\ 70_Network\ 71_WLAN_Report\ 80_Storage\
  90_App_Logs\

Every folder also contains a SOURCE.txt that records where its files came
from on this machine (source path, method, time, model and serial), so the
package can be checked against the original logs. Folders where mirroring
was incomplete also contain Skipped_Files.txt listing what was left out.

Every folder also contains browse.html, which shows that folder's text
content in a browser - no tools needed.

"Status: Skipped" means there was nothing to collect (for example no BSOD
has occurred). The reason is written to README.txt inside that folder.

6. Why there is no GB-sized memory file
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Two different things produce memory dumps:

1) Blue screen dumps - written by Windows itself, not by this tool.
   Whether you get a GB-sized file depends on "Write debugging information":
     Small memory dump    ~256 KB per crash, MEMORY.DMP is never created
     Kernel memory dump   MEMORY.DMP, usually 1-4 GB      <- usually enough
     Complete memory dump MEMORY.DMP, about the size of RAM
   To change it: This PC > Properties > Advanced system settings > Startup
   and Recovery > Settings > "Write debugging information". A reboot is
   required, and the file only appears after the next BSOD.
   The page file must also be large enough (system managed, or >= 16 GB),
   otherwise writing the dump fails.

2) Process memory dump - taken by this tool from a running process.
   The file appears immediately and is roughly the size of that process's
   memory (hundreds of MB to several GB).
   Use it for memory leaks, hangs, freezes, "slower the longer it runs".
   Tick "Process memory dump" and type the process name on the right
   (e.g. chrome.exe); leave it empty to dump the largest process.

If the symptom is "an app's memory keeps growing / it freezes", use 2).
If it is "blue screen / unexpected restart", use 1) after fixing the setting.

7. FAQ
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Q: The header says "Standard user: some items unavailable".
A: Click "Restart as administrator", or right-click the exe and choose
   "Run as administrator". Most items still work without admin.

Q: An item shows "Skipped" - is the tool broken?
A: No. Skipped means there was nothing to collect, for example no BSOD has
   occurred so there is no dump. The reason is in that folder's README.txt
   and also listed in the report.

Q: No dump collected for a BSOD
A: Check the dump setting printed in 30_Crash_Dumps\README.txt. Most often
   the system is set to "Small memory dump" or no BSOD has occurred yet.

Q: How long does a collection take?
A: About 1.5 minutes with the default items; about 3 minutes with everything
   (the energy report and performance sampling take a minute each).

Q: What are the actual sleep / hibernate timeouts?
A: See 41_Power_Settings\power_settings.txt or the "Power and sleep settings"
   table in the report. AC (plugged in) and DC (battery) are listed
   separately. "Never" means it does not trigger automatically.

8. Command line
----------------------------------------------------------------------
LogCollector.exe /cli /out:D:\logs /jobs:events-system,sysinfo,minidump
LogCollector.exe /cli /all /out:D:\logs /tag:SN1234567
LogCollector.exe /cli /out:D:\logs /jobs:pdump /proc:chrome.exe

Options: /cli no UI, /out output folder, /jobs comma separated item ids,
/all every item, /tag package name prefix, /case case id,
/symptom symptom text, /proc target process for the memory dump.

9. Notes
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- The tool only reads data. It does not clear logs, change settings or
  install anything.
- Reports and logs may contain personal data (user names, paths, SSIDs).
  Handle them according to your data classification policy.
- Process dumps can be large; watch the free disk space.
